title: The MLP block in nanoGPT
objective: Follow one token's vector through MLP.forward in model.py: c_fc widens it from n_embd to 4 * n_embd, GELU bends each value, and c_proj brings it back to n_embd.
audience_context: The learner is looking at the MLP class in nanoGPT's model.py (lines 78-92) and asked for a 30-second explanation of this code span. No other lesson concept is active.
scope_note: Dropout appears only as the final line in the order. How it behaves in training versus evaluation is left out, along with why the width factor is 4 and where the MLP sits in the transformer Block (residual connection and layer norm). The approved description covers only the two linear layers and the GELU, and the excerpt doesn't show the surrounding block.

evidence.excerpt:
class MLP(nn.Module):

    def __init__(self, config):
        super().__init__()
        self.c_fc    = nn.Linear(config.n_embd, 4 * config.n_embd, bias=config.bias)
        self.gelu    = nn.GELU()
        self.c_proj  = nn.Linear(4 * config.n_embd, config.n_embd, bias=config.bias)
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(config.dropout)

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.c_fc(x)
        x = self.gelu(x)
        x = self.c_proj(x)
        x = self.dropout(x)
        return x

claim_registry.text: self.c_fc = nn.Linear(config.n_embd, 4 * config.n_embd, bias=config.bias) is applied first in forward and widens each token's vector from n_embd values to 4 * n_embd values.
self.gelu = nn.GELU() is applied next, between the two linear layers. It is a fixed nonlinearity applied to each of the 4 * n_embd values separately, and it does not change the vector's size.
self.c_proj = nn.Linear(4 * config.n_embd, config.n_embd, bias=config.bias) projects the widened vector back to n_embd values, so the MLP's output has the same width as its input.
forward runs the steps in this order: x = self.c_fc(x), x = self.gelu(x), x = self.c_proj(x), x = self.dropout(x), return x.

Each nn.Linear acts on the last dimension of x, which is the n_embd-sized vector. The same weights are applied to every token's vector independently, so the MLP does not mix information between tokens.
The last step, self.dropout = nn.Dropout(config.dropout), is applied after c_proj, and the output keeps the same n_embd width.

must_show: The four forward lines from model.py (self.c_fc, self.gelu, self.c_proj, self.dropout), each highlighted in turn as its step runs
One token's vector labeled n_embd widening to a vector labeled 4 * n_embd at the c_fc step
Values in the widened vector reshaped one by one at the GELU step, with the width staying 4 * n_embd
The widened vector narrowing back to a vector labeled n_embd at the c_proj step
Several token vectors going through the same c_fc → gelu → c_proj path side by side without exchanging anything
The input and output vectors shown together at the same n_embd width at the end
must_not_claim: c_proj runs before c_fc, or GELU runs after c_proj
c_fc creates more tokens or lengthens the sequence instead of widening each token's vector
The MLP mixes or passes information between different tokens
GELU is a learned layer with its own weights
GELU sets every negative value to exactly zero
c_proj simply cuts off the extra 3 * n_embd values instead of computing a learned linear combination of all of them
The MLP output is 4 * n_embd wide
Dropout is part of the widening step
